title: Noun Phrases: One or More?
description: Learn how ka, ke, and nā help signal singular and plural noun phrases in common patterns.

sourceReview.notes: Source check, not educator review. Source spellings are normalized to Unicode ʻokina and NFC. Judd is not used to authorize any live form.

activities.instruction: Notice the singular noun phrase.
activities.prompt: Focus on the determiner before the noun.
activities.support: This example follows the general ka pattern.
activities.patternIntro: ka is the usual singular definite article before many nouns.
activities.languageNote: This is a noun phrase, not a complete sentence. The goal is to notice how number is signaled.

sourceRefs.section: Ka, Ke, Nā (Definite); Plurals; Nā Hamani

activities.instruction: Now change only the number.
activities.support: The noun stays the same; the determiner changes.
activities.patternIntro: nā marks a definite plural noun phrase.
activities.languageNote: Plural meaning can be carried by the determiner even when the noun form itself does not change.

sourceRefs.section: Ka, Ke, Nā (Definite); Plurals; Nā Hamani

activities.instruction: See the usual ke pattern.
activities.support: The modern reference grammar gives this exact example.
activities.patternIntro: As a general rule, ke is used before words beginning with k, a, e, or o.
activities.languageNote: This is a general rule, not an exception-free formula. Some nouns take ke outside that simple pattern.

sourceRefs.section: Ka, Ke, Nā (Definite); Plurals; Nā Hamani

activities.instruction: Make the noun phrase plural.
activities.prompt: Compare ke kao with nā kao.
activities.support: The noun stays the same; the determiner signals plural.
activities.patternIntro: nā replaces singular ka/ke when the noun phrase is definite plural.
activities.languageNote: Listen for nā because it can immediately change how many participants or things are being discussed.

activities.instruction: Use the noun phrase inside a familiar sentence.
activities.prompt: Ua ʻai ʻo ia i ka poi.
activities.support: What does ka poi tell you about the noun phrase here?
options: It is a singular definite noun phrase
It refers to three or more people
It marks the sentence as a question
activities.answer: It is a singular definite noun phrase
activities.explanation: ka is a singular definite determiner in ka poi.
